name: Abilene Christian University
fc_current_name: Department of Art and Design
fc_current_chair: Robert Green (Professor; Department Chair and Program Director, Fine Art). Graphic Design directed by Ryan Feerer.
fc_current_status: The Department of Art and Design (College of Arts and Sciences) is active and offers a BFA in Art with concentrations in Studio Art, Graphic Design, and All-Level Teaching, plus majors in Art Education, Art Therapy, Graphic Design, and Interior Architecture and Design. Studio Art concentration tracks are Ceramics, Painting, and Sculpture only. There is NO metals/jewelry/metalsmithing concentration, major, or listed ART course in the current catalog. The department still advertises facilities including "a well-equipped metal casting foundry" and metalworking pneumatic tools, but these now serve sculpture/foundry rather than a jewelry/silversmithing program.
fc_what_happened: The metals/jewelry/silversmithing program was effectively the personal program of Virginia "Ginna" Sadler, who taught at ACU from 1980 until her retirement in 2016 (36 years). She held an MFA in jewelry design and silversmithing from Indiana University (1974) and was a member of the Society of North American Goldsmiths (SNAG). After her 2016 retirement the dedicated metals/jewelry teaching was not continued — current Studio Art concentrations are Ceramics, Painting, and Sculpture, with no metals/jewelry courses or specialist faculty. Sadler was named professor emeritus and died March 12, 2023, at age 74. The archived directory entry ("Ginna Sadler 1980 to present") reflects the pre-2016 state; the program did not survive her departure.

Classes run continuously through 2025–2026. Leadership of the Jewelry/Metals Department is now Robin Servo (20+ years at BBAC); the archived faculty member Robert C. Fisher is no longer listed anywhere. Other current metals instructors include Nancy Clark, Janice Degen, Darlene Earls, and Mary Kernahan.

The archived directory record carried no start date or faculty for this entry, and the program may have been listed loosely or have predated CSUN's online catalogs (earliest available, 2014, already shows no metals/jewelry concentration). Across the 2014, 2018, and current (2025/26) Art catalogs, the concentration list has been stable and never includes metals or jewelry; only Sculpture/Ceramics relate to 3D making, and Graphic Design is the only concentration noted as suspended. name: Memphis College of Art
fc_current_status: degrees offered now, dept it sits in
fc_what_happened: The metals/jewelry program closed when the entire institution shut down. Memphis College of Art (founded 1936) announced in October 2017 that it would stop recruiting new students due to mounting real estate debt, a small endowment, and declining enrollment (down ~35% that year). It operated on a teach-out plan and closed permanently at the end of the 2019-20 academic year, holding its final commencement on May 9, 2020 (conducted virtually due to COVID-19). Metalworking/jewelry was one of MCA's 16 fine-arts programs (11 undergraduate BFA + 5 graduate degrees). There is no successor academic metals program. Note: in May 2022 the unrelated Metal Museum signed a lease for MCA's former campus (Rust Hall in Overton Park) — this is a museum/exhibition institution, NOT a continuation of the degree-granting academic program.

name: Metairie Park Country Day School
fc_current_name: Metairie Park Country Day School — Visual Arts (Metals)
fc_current_status: Not a degree-granting institution. This is a K-12 independent private school in Metairie, Louisiana. "Metals" continues to exist as a semester-long Upper School (grades 9-12) visual-arts elective within the Visual Arts program (alongside Ceramics, Woodworking, 2D Art, Photography); metalworking is also taught in Middle School. No college degrees are offered — credential is a high school diploma.
fc_what_happened: The metals/jewelry course continues as part of the school's Visual Arts curriculum. The archived directory's named faculty member, Vitrice McMurry (listed "1983 to present"), is no longer in the current MPCDS faculty directory and is now described in external sources as a FORMER metals teacher at the school — i.e., a leadership/teacher change since ~2014. She taught metalworking two days a week to grades 6-12 from 1983 for many years; she remains active as an independent New Orleans jewelry designer (sold at Symmetry Jewelers, Ogden Museum, NOMA; former Jazz Fest crafts director). The current metals teacher is not publicly named on the school site. Note: the archived record's framing as an academic "metals/jewelry PROGRAM" overstates it — it was always a secondary-school art elective, never a collegiate metals/jewelry/CAD-CAM degree program.

The metals/jewelry program itself was not closed, merged, or renamed: post-2014 it continues as an active concentration in the Studio Art BA/BFA, with graduate study and a Jewelry Design & Metals minor still offered as of 2025–26. I could not confirm by name the specific tenured metals faculty member who succeeded Ewing or the current Department of Art chair.

name: Middle Tennessee State University
fc_current_name: Department of Art and Design, Middle Tennessee State University
fc_current_chair: Jimmy Mumford (Chair, Department of Art and Design, as of 2025)
fc_current_status: No metals/jewelry/metalsmithing concentration is offered today. The Department of Art and Design (College of Liberal Arts) offers a BFA in Studio Art with emphases in ceramics, painting, printmaking, or sculpture; plus BFA Graphic Design, BS/BA Visual Arts, BS/BA Art History, and BS Art Education. Kallenberger — the program's metals/jewelry/silversmithing professor (MFA jewelry & silversmithing, Univ. of Kansas; he designed MTSU's ceremonial maces and chain of office) — taught roughly 1966 to 2002 and RETIRED in 2002 after 36 years. There is no evidence the metals/jewelry teaching area continued under a successor. By the present-day Department of Art and Design, the studio BFA emphases are ceramics, painting, printmaking, and sculpture only; no metals/jewelry concentration exists. So the program effectively ended with Kallenberger's 2002 retirement rather than surviving as a degree path; it was not renamed or merged into a continuing metals concentration.

The program's metal-focused craft activity now lives inside the Engraving Arts concentration (which ESU markets as the world's only engraving BFA). Separately, ESU underwent a major 2022 restructuring under President Ken Hush (33 faculty/staff terminated Sept 2022, multiple programs suspended; AAUP investigated), followed by a publicized "Reinvestment in Art" initiative (new hires, King Hall renovations). Engraving program leader James Ehlers chaired Art through 2024 then moved to Baylor; leadership has changed since.

fc_current_status: No metals/jewelry program exists. The organization closed in 2009. It was a community art center, never a degree-granting academic program. NOTE: This is a distinct institution from Florida Gulf Coast University (FGCU) in Fort Myers, which is unrelated and offers a general Art BA (painting/drawing/sculpture/ceramics/printmaking/photography) with no dedicated metalsmithing/jewelry degree.
fc_what_happened: Closed. The Florida Gulf Coast Art Center was a non-degree community art center in Belleair, FL (roots to the Belleair Arts Center, ~1936; long-running facility on land donated 1944, built 1948). It ran art classes/workshops and, in the 1980s, partnered with the Florida Society of Goldsmiths (FSG) on art-metal/jewelry workshops and the first exhibition of art-metal jewelry by Florida artists (May 1986). In 1999 the organization relocated to Pinewood Cultural Park in Largo, FL and was renamed the Gulf Coast Museum of Art. Facing severe financial pressure, the Gulf Coast Museum of Art closed in January 2009. Its permanent collection (contemporary Florida art) was transferred to St. Petersburg College (Florida International Museum), and the Largo building later became The Gallery at Creative Pinellas. The closure (2009) predates the directory's ~2014 offline window, so by the archived snapshot the program no longer existed.

fc_what_happened: The program has continued without closure, merger, or renaming. The institution's full name is now "Massachusetts College of Art and Design" (MassArt). Since ~2014 the most notable change is faculty turnover: Joseph Wood (archived as "1986 to present") is no longer listed as core/tenure-line J&M faculty — he now appears only as a Visiting Lecturer in directory listings. Emily Cobb has become the principal Associate Professor in Jewelry & Metalsmithing, bringing a digital-fabrication / CAD-CAM emphasis. Visiting lecturers (Venetia Dale, Joyce Kutty) round out the area.
fc_current_faculty: Heather White (Professor, Jewelry and Metalsmithing (3D Arts); Metals Department Coordinator); Emily Cobb (Associate Professor, Jewelry and Metalsmithing); Venetia Dale (Visiting Lecturer, Jewelry and Metalsmithing); Joyce Kutty (Visiting Lecturer, Jewelry and Metalsmithing); Julia Gaitley (Studio Manager, Jewelry and Metalsmithing)

name: Southern Illinois University
fc_current_name: Metalsmithing, School of Art and Design, Southern Illinois University Carbondale
fc_current_chair: No single "metals program head" is published; the program is staffed by Rick (Richard E.) Smith, Professor — blacksmithing, and Sun Kyoung Kim, Associate Professor — small metals/jewelry. Smith effectively oversees the blacksmithing side. (Overall unit leadership = the School of Art and Design director, not specifically published on the metals page.)
fc_current_status: Active and thriving. Offers a BFA in Studio Art: Metalsmithing (120 cr) and an MFA in Art with two metals tracks: Blacksmithing and Small Metals (60 cr min). SIU bills itself as the only MFA blacksmithing program in the nation. The program sits in the School of Art and Design, within the College of Arts and Media (web-branded under "Art, Architecture, and Design"). The studios are in the historic Pulliam Industrial/Design wing (blacksmithing studio, plus jewelry/small-metals and casting spaces).
fc_what_happened: Continuation with a generational faculty handoff. The program founded by L. Brent Kington (began rebuilding SIU metals after 1961; "reintroduced blacksmithing as an art form to the US"; Lifetime Achievement, SNAG 2011; the $1M endowed L. Brent Kington chair was created in 2006) and Richard Mawdsley (fine metals, from 1978) is now carried by Rick Smith (blacksmithing) and Sun Kyoung Kim (small metals/jewelry). Mawdsley and Kington are emeritus/deceased. Since ~2014 the program has continued uninterrupted, retaining both blacksmithing and small-metals/jewelry tracks at BFA and MFA levels; the academic unit has been reorganized/rebranded into the School of Art and Design under the College of Arts and Media.
fc_current_faculty: Rick Smith (Professor (Metalsmithing/Blacksmithing)); Sun Kyoung Kim (Associate Professor (Metals/Jewelry))
